Package io.mavlink4j.service

Class RequestResponse

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.service.RequestResponse
public final class RequestResponse extends Object
The shared Family-A state machine (see docs/API.md): send X, await a reply matching a MatchKey within a deadline, retry up to N times on silence, and let a reply itself decide whether the exchange is done or should keep waiting a bit longer without a resend. Command, Parameter and the future Mission and FTP services are all instances of this one shape, differing only in timeout/retry numbers and in how they build a payload and read a reply. This class is deliberately generic over both: it is built once, here, as a standalone collaborator that CommandService constructs and drives, not as a private helper folded into it.

Why continuation-based, not thread-blocking

Every step is chained via CompletableFuture.thenCompose(java.util.function.Function<? super T, ? extends java.util.concurrent.CompletionStage<U>>)/exceptionallyCompose rather than a thread parked on Future#get. A Correlator's own waiter future already completes asynchronously (matched by the RX thread that decoded the reply, or timed out by the JDK's own delay scheduler — see DefaultCorrelator) — chaining onto it costs no thread of our own, which matters because a broker-driven caller may have many exchanges in flight at once and must not pay one blocked thread per outstanding command.

Duplicate replies are idempotent for free. Correlator.await(io.mavlink4j.session.MatchKey, java.time.Duration)'s returned future is consumed exactly once per registration and the key is released the moment it completes — a second, late arrival of the same reply after this exchange has already moved on finds no live waiter and is silently dropped by Correlator's own implementation. This class adds no de-duplication of its own because none is needed.

A note on which thread a continuation runs on

CompletableFuture callbacks run, by default, on whichever thread completes the upstream stage. A Correlator waiter is completed directly from the MavlinkSession reader thread that decoded the matching frame (see that class's javadoc) — so a retry resend, or a re-registration after a reply that only extended the deadline, can execute synchronously on that RX thread rather than a thread of the caller's choosing. This is accepted deliberately: retries and extensions are rare compared to the hot per-frame dispatch path Dispatcher's own must-not-block rule exists to protect, and a UDP FrameSink.send(java.lang.Object, io.mavlink4j.PeerId) is normally non-blocking. A caller that cannot accept this (e.g. wants every continuation off the RX thread) can wrap the FrameSink/Correlator it hands to this class, or chain further with the Async variants of CompletableFuture outside this class — not done here to avoid needing an Executor this module has no opinion about.

    RequestResponse.ReplyClassifier
    Classifies a reply that matched the MatchKey: null means the reply is terminal (the exchange completes with it); a non-null, positive Duration means "keep waiting on the same key for this long, without resending" (Family-A's IN_PROGRESS-style continuation).

  • Method Details

    • exchange

      public CompletableFuture<Frame> exchange(PeerId target, MatchKey key, Duration timeout, int maxRetries, RequestResponse.AttemptPayload payload, RequestResponse.ReplyClassifier classifier)
      Runs one Family-A exchange: sends payload.forAttempt(0) to target, awaits a reply matching key within timeout. A reply hands control to classifier: a null verdict completes the returned future with that reply; a Duration verdict re-awaits the same key for that long, without resending. Silence (no reply of any kind within timeout) retries — a fresh send via payload.forAttempt(n) — up to maxRetries times; once exhausted, the returned future fails with the TimeoutException the last attempt's wait ended with.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxRetries is negative
